author: Autodesk
description: A gel torus with checkboard material smashes into the ground
documentation:
## Gel Checker Graph

### Description

This graph shows how to use fields to set spatially varying material properties for the MPM solver.  It also shows how to separate the out the particles based on a property and create a surface mesh for rendering each of them. The meshes created in this way are not suitable for refractive rendering as is, they contain many internal intersections.

### Inputs, Controls & Outputs

The main control for this graph is a torus mesh that controls the location, shape, and size of the gel material. The `source_gel_checker` compound can also be edited to control which properties are varied.  The `checker_field_` can be edited or replaced with any field that takes the values zero and one to distinguish spatial locations.

The output of this graph are two meshes ready to be rendered with Arnold. The points from the MPM simulation have been split based on the checker property and converted into two levelsets, then converted into polygon meshes. The example also includes a `standard_surface_mat` that is wired into an `assign_material` node to define a gel material for the mesh. The gel material utilizes subsurface scattering and a shiny coat to approximate wax.

### Workflow and Tips

The `file_cache` compound is not required. However, it is strongly recommended to cache out the MPM particles. Do note for efficiency there is an `erase_component_properties` compound before the `file_cache` compound to reduce the file size as many properties are not required outside of the simulation. It also makes it very easy to iterate on the meshing and render settings without having to worry about losing a simulation result once everything is dialed in. Also, once cached, the rendering could be easily distributed to a render farm if that is available.

values.name: erase_component_properties.properties
values.value: point_hardening  point_velocity_gradient point_age point_dead point_viscosity point_elastic_strain point_mass point_vibration_speed point_volume_preservation

_notes.text:
Render settings:

On the Bifrost shape node, it is ideal that one set:
Arnold --> Translator Options --> Motion blur mode: Velocity Only

This ensures the quickest translate time since the renderer will only be able to use the point_velocity property stored on the mesh.

Arnold:

AA - 5
Diffuse - 3
Specular - 1
Transmission - 1
SSS - 3
Volume Indirect - 1


Motion Blur (Enable)

The file_cache is set to passthrough.
When running the simulation at production resolution it is ideal to cache out the simulation data before rendering, as typically the render will take longer than the simulation and can be easily resumed (unlike the simulation)
